data.current_summary: Subscribe a callback URL to dispatch lifecycle events
data.current_description: HTTPS callback. Returns the signing secret once. Deliveries carry X-Scope-Signature (v1=HMAC_SHA256(secret, timestamp + '.' + body)), X-Scope-Event-Id (idempotency), X-Scope-Timestamp. The body is { id, type, occurred_at, tenant_id, scope_id, data }. For type 'dispatch.pending_approval', data carries scope_id, display_id, approval_id, triggered_rules, computed_price_cents (the professional's price), vendor_id (the professional's organization) and auto_escalate_after_minutes. Beside the professional's price, five fields say what the firm will be billed if it approves. firm_total_cents (integer or null): the estimated firm total, the professional's price plus Scope's fee line, computed with the invoice's own arithmetic on the terms on file now; null when Scope cannot determine the fee before the job is sent. scope_fee_cents (integer or null): Scope's fee line as it would be billed; null when firm_total_cents is null. scope_fee_label (string): the invoice line Scope's fee appears under, "Service coordination and compliance record". firm_total_is_estimate (boolean or null): true whenever firm_total_cents is a number, because the amount billed is set when the job is sent (for example, the professional's current rates apply then); null when firm_total_cents is null. billing_note (string): one sentence for a person: the estimated firm total with the invoice's two lines and why it can move; or the professional's price and the sentence that Scope's fee is added on the invoice; or, when Scope could not read the price, that sentence alone. These fields describe the bill; they do not change what is approved or sent.
data.description_suggestion: Creates a webhook subscription to receive dispatch lifecycle events via HTTPS callback. The subscription returns a signing secret (returned once only) used to verify webhook authenticity. Webhook deliveries include X-Scope-Signature (HMAC_SHA256 signature), X-Scope-Event-Id (for idempotency), and X-Scope-Timestamp headers. Event payload structure: { id, type, occurred_at, tenant_id, scope_id, data }. For dispatch.pending_approval events, data includes scope_id, display_id, approval_id, triggered_rules, computed_price_cents (professional's price), vendor_id, auto_escalate_after_minutes, and billing fields (firm_total_cents, scope_fee_cents, scope_fee_label, firm_total_is_estimate, billing_note). Billing fields are informational and do not affect approval or dispatch. Requires appropriate authorization scope. Tenant-scoped and audit-logged.
data.reasoning: Summary is clear and action-oriented. Description is extremely dense and difficult to parse. Improved version reorganizes information hierarchically: subscription mechanics first, then signature verification details, then event structure, then dispatch-specific payload details. Clarifies that billing fields are informational. Better structured for AI agent comprehension of when to use this operation and what to expect.
